calculation.scope: Arithmetic of the displayed rates, not a new causal estimate or assertion that rounded rates are exact underlying rates.

correction: The stated seven-unit rise is 12.5%of the 2015 base 56, not 14.3%. The comparison remains an increase. Official Destatis tables confirm the displayed rates; the RKI historical table reports 2015 as 56.0 to one decimal, which also limits a benign rounding explanation.
effect: Slightly weakens the magnitude used in the argument that rising abortions show no need to expand provision. It does not establish whether access is adequate; national totals alone do not settle regional barriers.
limits: The absolute counts and upward direction are not refuted. No calculation is shown; a clerical or denominator slip is possible. Published rates are rounded and census-based population series can change. This record corrects the arithmetic of the displayed 56-to 63 comparison rather than deriving an exact harmonised 2015-2024 trend. Historical RKI 2015 rate 56.0 means a hidden rate near 55.5 cannot rescue 14.3%while retaining a 2024 rate rounded to 63. No clinical-risk conclusion or optimal-policy conclusion follows.
materiality_explanation: Minor: growth is overstated by 1.8 percentage points, while the same national upward trend remains. The opposition also invokes legal, moral, clinical and counselling arguments, which this arithmetic check does not decide.
direction_explanation: A larger growth figure adds support to the national-abundance premise supporting rejection. The direction is distinct from limited materiality. No intent is inferred.

confidence.text_source_mismatch: high for arithmetic of the displayed figures

context_checked: Read all 12 pages, including the national counts onpp 5-6, supply-adequacy inference immediately after the calculation, account of counselling experiences and final explicit request onp 12.
The denominator is expressly women aged 15 to under 50; no pregnancy/recipient denominator conflation alleged. The separate percentage among live births plus abortions is outside this issue.
Destatis identifies rates based on resident women and different census-based population series from 2024. Preserve comparability context without inflating it into another proved error.
National count increases alone prove neither adequate provision nor shortage. This inference is discussed as effect, not alleged as a separate fact error.

Independent tax reviewer checked the current Destatis table date(28 April 2026)against the 14 Aprilsubmission. Treat this later retrieval as reference-year corroboration, not an authenticated contemporaneous webpage. The stated-figure arithmetic and earlierRKI 2015 precision are the core check.
